extraction.Name: Richard Stirk, Jr.
extraction.Refused/Protested: did not want his patent to his allotment for the reason that he knew how hard it would be to pay the taxes; but his farmer told him that it would be recorded just the same, and that he would have the taxes to pay, so he accepted the patent
extraction.Sold/Mortgaged: he never sold or mortgaged this land; but he deeded it over to his wife, March 1, 1921; that, on March 31, 1928, she deeded it back to him
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: There are some taxes now due on the place, but that is the only encumbrance. The reason for the transfer of this land was on account of getting into debt so heavily at the time, and he went through bankruptcy.
extraction.Occupation/Income: his only source of income is what he raises on this allotment and by doing odd jobs, such as road work
extraction.NOTES: Document No. 2667; subscribed and sworn before a notary public on November 13, 1928; deponent is mentally competent and in good possession of good health; has a wife and 5 minor children to support, all in good health; has never received any aid from the County or Government; he was not conversant with the law on this matter as to the land being exempt on these debts; at present the only debts are the aforementioned taxes | TASK 5 BULK ALLOTMENT RECOVERY 2026-04-29: Sonnet text-extraction captured the allotment number from the source page header but classified it in NOTES as a 'document number' / 'Document No.' / 'No. NNNN' instead of placing it in the structured Allotment number field. The hypothesis that these document/file references are actually allotment numbers was confirmed via BLM cross-reference (exemplars: Eugene Means 2249, Lucy Patton 6802).
